claim.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve

roles.L0/N1877+: Count-word neuron: fires on ' seven' and on the query ' twelve'; marks the last token as a bare count word that wants a counted noun.
roles.L0/N1277+: Count-word neuron, as N1877; the strongest single count marker at ' twelve' (largest patch effect when ' twelve' becomes ' the').
roles.L0/N1108+: Count-word neuron at ' seven' and ' twelve'.
roles.L0/N141+: Count-word neuron at ' seven' and ' twelve'.
roles.L0/N1654+: Count-word neuron at ' seven' and ' twelve'.
roles.L0/N1669+: Count/quantity-word neuron; its value at the count-word positions is what flips when the count word is replaced by a determiner.
roles.L0/N883+: Count-word neuron; adds to the count marking at ' twelve'.
roles.L0/N1101+: Time-unit neuron: writes the identity of ' days' (and ' week', ' year') at their positions, the content the copy heads later read.
roles.L0/H0: Early context head; builds the clause frame '<a> <time unit> has <count>' at both clauses so the two clauses line up.
roles.L0/H2: Early head, strong on determiners near the start ('A', ' a'); marks the start of each 'a X has' clause.
roles.L1/H1: Layer-1 head that carries the clause/position frame forward; needed for the copy heads to find ' days' (sufficiency).
roles.L1/H6: Broad copy head: averages the earlier context (' week', ' seven', ' days') into each later position, giving the query at ' twelve' the parallel-clause context.
roles.L1/H7: Broad head that attends to the structural anchor ('has') before the count word and writes 'count word after has' at ' seven' and ' twelve'.
roles.L3/N456+: Count-word neuron in the middle layers: re-marks ' twelve' as a count word after the early heads.
roles.L3/N1350+: Mid-layer neuron that boosts the counted-noun prediction at the query position.
roles.L3/H3: Induction-style copy head: from ' twelve' it attends to ' days', the token that followed the earlier count word ' seven', and writes ' days' to the last position.
roles.L4/H0: Second copy head; reinforces the move of ' days' to the last position.
roles.L4/H7: Copy head that moves the ' days' identity to the last position, after L3/H3.
roles.L5/H7: Late head that keeps the 'count word wants a noun' reading at the last position.
roles.L5/N1617+: Output neuron that pushes counted plural nouns (' days') up.
roles.L5/N207+: Output neuron that pushes counted nouns up.
roles.L5/N2036-: Negative pole that pushes down layout and function tokens ('.', ',', ' and') after the count word.
roles.L5/N575-: Negative pole that pushes down layout tokens after the count word.
roles.L5/N119-: Negative pole that pushes down layout tokens after the count word.

claim.explanation: A copy route keyed on the query count word. Layer-0 count-word neurons fire on ' seven' and on the final ' twelve'; time-unit neurons write the identity of ' days'. Layer-0 and layer-1 heads line up the two parallel 'a X has <count>' clauses. At ' twelve', the induction-style head L3/H3, with L4/H0 and L4/H7, attends to ' days' (the noun that followed the earlier count word) and copies it to the last position. Layer-5 neurons push a counted noun up and layout tokens down; they do not choose between ' days' and ' months', so the copied ' days' wins over the fact that a year has twelve months. The route needs a count word at the end: replace ' twelve' with a determiner (' the') and the count neurons go quiet, the copy does not fire, and the answer leaves ' days'. Swap the count word for another number and ' days' stays; swap the copied noun and the answer follows it.
claim.corrupted: A week has seven days and a year has the

counterfactuals.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has ten
counterfactuals.why: Source swap at the query: ' ten' is still a count word, so the count neurons fire and the heads copy ' days'.

counterfactuals.prompt: A week has 7 days and a year has 12
counterfactuals.why: Digits instead of number words: still count tokens before and after, so the same copy of ' days' runs.

counterfactuals.prompt: A month has thirty days and a year has twelve
counterfactuals.why: Source swap of the first count word and the time unit: ' days' still follows a count word, so it is still copied.

counterfactuals.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has the
counterfactuals.why: The query is a determiner, not a count word: the count neurons are off at the last position and the copy does not fire.

counterfactuals.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has many
counterfactuals.why: ' many' is a quantity word but not a number; the count-word marking at the last position is weak, so ' days' is not copied to the top.

counterfactuals.prompt: A week has seven hours and a year has twelve
counterfactuals.why: Swap of the copied noun: the heads copy the token after ' seven', now ' hours', so ' hours' replaces ' days'.

counterfactuals.prompt: A spider has eight legs and a dog has four
counterfactuals.why: Same frame, other domain: the route copies ' legs', the noun after the first count word.

prompts.prompt: In a calendar, a week has seven days and a year has twelve
prompts.why: Extra words between the clauses; the count word is still last and days still follows the earlier count word.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days, and a year has twelve
prompts.why: Comma changes layout; the route should still copy days.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a leap year has twelve
prompts.why: Different subject modifier in the second clause; copy head should still find days.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days while a century has twelve
prompts.why: Different connective and different subject; count word is last, copy should fire.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has eleven
prompts.why: Another number word swaps in; the claim says days stays.

prompts.prompt: A fortnight has fourteen days and a year has twelve
prompts.why: Different source count word and a different first subject; days still follows the count word.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twenty
prompts.why: Another count word; the claim predicts days stays.

prompts.prompt: Everyone knows a week has seven days and a year has twelve
prompts.why: Distractor prefix; the clause frame is unchanged.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has about twelve
prompts.why: Adverb before the count word; count word still last.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven nights and a year has twelve
prompts.why: Swap the copied noun; the answer should follow nights, so days is not top.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven weekdays and a year has twelve
prompts.why: Copied noun is replaced by weekdays; the answer follows the copy.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve months and a decade has ten
prompts.why: Earlier clause now gives months as the noun after a count word; the copy points elsewhere (years or months).

prompts.prompt: A year has twelve months and a week has seven
prompts.why: Order reversed so the noun after the earlier count word is months; the copy gives months, not days.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve months and a month has thirty
prompts.why: Context now shows months after twelve; the induction copy should point to months or days only by prior.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has a
prompts.why: Determiner at the end instead of a count word; the route says the copy does not fire.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has some
prompts.why: Quantifier but not a bare count word; the claim says count neurons go quiet.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve of
prompts.why: Count word is no longer the last token; next token should be 'the' or similar, not days.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve.
prompts.why: Sentence ends with a period, so the next token is layout, not a counted noun.

prompts.prompt: There are seven days in a week and twelve
prompts.why: Different frame; days comes before the count word, not after it, so the induction copy has no target and months is likely.

prompts.prompt: Twelve months make a year and seven
prompts.why: Count word comes first and is followed by months; copy points to months, and the frame is different.

prompts.prompt: The number twelve is written as 12. A week has seven days and a year has twelve
prompts.why: Distractor mentions twelve earlier with no noun after it; the route keys on seven followed by days.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven days and a year has twelve days and a month has thirty
prompts.why: Context repeats days after count words; the copy should still give days.

prompts.prompt: A week has seven colours and a year has twelve
prompts.why: The copied noun is colours; the answer should follow it, not days.

prompts.prompt: A tricycle has three wheels and a year has twelve
prompts.why: Noun after the earlier count word is wheels; the copy should point to wheels.
